coverage_note: No CHAT lines in this lesson. From 24:49 on most of Medi's Arabic is Latin-transliterated (badhak ala, barja, safri ...). Lines 44:57-47:13 show only Amal (Medi's attempts at the go-home command are missing, probably mislabeled), so 46:36 has no medi_said. Engine: تيس = تسع (55:46); واسكت/اسكت 41:01 and oskot 1:02:43 are accepted by Amal (عادي), not errors. Names not flagged: عمان (03:21, engine garble), الفلسطينيين, Palestine. Left out as not errors: 02:22-02:44 false starts, 12:xx English politics, 29:48 Idhaki (right), 30:51 daheki (right), 1:03:52 safi (Amal confirms), 1:04 اقلقي (ق dropped, S4), 1:10 goodbye. Echo-candidates file for 10-28 does not exist.

rows.medi_said: It's بعيد, right? بعيد.
rows.why: He asked how to say 'I removed (the apps)' and offered بعيد (far); Amal answered with إمت (her word as the engine wrote it) and used it again at 05:06 'لما إمت الـ Instagram'.
rows.english: I removed / deleted Instagram and the games

rows.medi_said: Do you guys use enough كافية? Is, uh، is this an Arabic word or no?
rows.why: He asked whether كافية is used; Amal supplied بكفي (didn't-know).

rows.medi_said: كل اليوم مش-- uh، ما عندي بكافية وقت.
rows.why: The adjective goes after its noun (وقت بكفي); Amal re-said it in that order.

rows.medi_said: Yeah، راح يسعد. Yeah، راح يسعدني. [unintelligible] It
rows.why: يسعد means make happy; he meant 'it will help (me)' and Amal gave يساعد. (He self-fixed أسعدني to يسعدني before her; the fixed version is what she corrected.)

rows.medi_said: كل إشي بيحر-- كل إشي بيحرك.
rows.amal_said: بيت حرك. ... لا، بيت is you getting moved. So كل إشي gets moved.
rows.why: He used the make-X form (بيحرك, moves something) where 'everything is moving' needs the get-X form بيتحرك; Amal named it and he echoed بيت حرك.

rows.medi_said: شوب، uh، بين، بينو، بينهم.
rows.why: He reached for 'in between' (neither cold nor hot) with بينهم; Amal confirmed it and supplied نص نص, which he repeated. Help on the way, so low.

rows.medi_said: بدك، بدك المطر؟
rows.why: He asked 'do you want the rain?' meaning 'do you like the rain'; Amal answered with بحب and he took it ('بتحب, yeah').

rows.medi_said: الفلسطينيين، uh، ناخد المطر؟ المي؟
rows.why: 'Take' (ناخد) for 'collect' rainwater; Amal did not understand (كيف يعني؟) and he fell back to English. Right form is my best reading.

rows.medi_said: الفلسطينيين، uh، ناخد المطر؟ المي؟
rows.why: The subject is 'the Palestinians' (they) but the verb is the we-form ناخد.

rows.medi_said: أنا جربت بس الـ set، uh, يخرب، uh, يخرب-- يخرب-- يخرب؟
rows.why: He used the present/jussive يخرب where he needed the past (the cards broke); Amal recast خربه and he named خربوا as what he meant ('It's not a verb').
rows.english: The cards got messed up / broke

rows.medi_said: بنت به. Uh, بنت به. ... is to, to take care of something.
rows.amal_said: Actually، بنتبه is more like pay attention.
rows.why: He defined بنتبه as 'take care of something'; Amal corrected the meaning to pay attention (انتبه = pay attention).

rows.medi_said: أنا نسيت.
rows.why: He could not find the verb for 'practice' (asked if it is a new verb, أنا نسيت) and Amal supplied بتدرب.

rows.medi_said: بتدرب لا؟
rows.why: Amal asked what بتدرب takes; his guess was لا and she gave على (the verb picks its own preposition).

rows.medi_said: Great. تمارنتي
rows.why: Asked for a command sentence he gave a non-command form and Amal said only أمر; no clean fix was voiced, she dropped it at 23:27 (خلص طيب ماشي).

rows.medi_said: جب على. [laughs] جب لا.
rows.amal_said: لا، لا، لا. ... Bring it to me.
rows.why: For 'bring to someone' he tried جب على / جب لا; Amal said no three times and cued 'Bring it to me'; the fix at 25:16 is جبيلي إياه (the person rides on لـ as an ending).

rows.medi_said: بيجيب اللي. ... بيجيب اللي أي. Yeah.
rows.amal_said: جبيلي إياه. Why did you put be؟
rows.why: The task was a command but he used the present form with b- (engine: بيجيب اللي أي = bijibli iyyaah); Amal gave جبيلي إياه and asked why he put b-. She praised his إياه.

rows.medi_said: you prank your cousins, you badhak alayha?
rows.amal_said: Mm-hmm. Or it could be more serious...
rows.why: 'Cousins' is plural but he used the she-pronoun ending (alayha); Amal let it pass.

rows.medi_said: Trump hadeekna, tehekna
rows.why: He tried 'Trump fooled us' with an ending on the verb (-na); Amal prompted the past verb ضحك twice and he reached tehekalayna (ضحك علينا), the verb's preposition plus ending.

rows.medi_said: harb jadeed. Jadeeda.
rows.amal_said: We didn't learn the plural for حرب. ... حروب.
rows.why: Meaning 'no new wars' he said the singular harb; Amal reminded him they had not learned the plural of حرب and gave حروب (he guessed durus/uruk first).

rows.medi_said: Okay, but if you're like complaining to your mudir, it would be ala.
rows.amal_said: على؟ لا. The على is about someone, against someone. ... لـ المدير.
rows.why: For complaining TO the manager he proposed على; Amal said لا and gave لـ المدير (على is against someone).

rows.medi_said: so sa, uh, safri
rows.why: He gave the command without the long vowel (safri); Amal recast سافري and said 'you should say سافري' (long A, so no إ). Pronunciation-family bucket, filed per brief.

rows.medi_said: Hadik al-dawla, uh, is, uh, biddik jibal.
rows.why: 'If you like mountains' came without el-; Amal recast الجبال (and confirmed plural جبال, singular جبل). He asked 'what did I say?'.

rows.medi_said: I don't know how to say surprise.
rows.why: English word in an Arabic sentence (oskut an el-hafle ashan ... surprise); he asked and Amal supplied مفاجأة.

rows.medi_said: imta barawe min safar, um, when are you gonna leave from your trip?
rows.amal_said: Gonna come back from your trip.
rows.why: Amal's sentence had min el-safar; he repeated it without el-. She let it pass (she only translated 'come back from your trip').
rows.english: when are you going home from the trip?

rows.medi_said: (his attempt is not in the transcript)
rows.amal_said: it's a wrong form. Let's go back home. ... La la. Right verb, but wrong command form. We said it's a double, it's a double W. So rawahi.
rows.wrong: (his attempt is not in the transcript)
rows.why: Amal says right verb, wrong command form and gives rawahi, but Medi's own line is missing (lines 44:57-47:13 show only Amal), so the wrong piece is unknown.

rows.medi_said: But what is it for you feminine? Is it nisti?
rows.amal_said: Nseeti because, because you is nseed. So you feminine is...
rows.why: He asked/guessed the feminine past of نسي as nisti; Amal gave nseeti with the rule (you-fem = stem + -ti) and he repeated nesiti. A question, so medium.

rows.medi_said: Would I say تيس على تيس؟
rows.why: Engine wrote تيس for تسعة (S4); for 'around nine' he put no el- on the number and Amal recast على التسع with el-.

rows.medi_said: على. And that one is logical. Oh my God.
rows.amal_said: Keep quiet on. ... Or about. ... عن.
rows.why: Quizzed on بسكت (keep quiet about) he answered على; Amal gave عن.

rows.medi_said: Uh, like quiet about how much it costs? I thought hat was costs.
rows.wrong: quiet about how much it costs
rows.why: He read حق as 'cost' in ما بسكت عن حقي; Amal said no and led him to 'rights'.
rows.english: I won't keep quiet about my rights

rows.medi_said: Uh, khafi, khafi.
rows.why: Asked for the command 'scare me' (make-X) he gave the get-scared command khafi; Amal said no and accepted khawafni / خوفني (doubled middle).

rows.medi_said: لا تمرين، لا، لا وقت مع ... بعاد وقت مع عائلتي.
rows.why: 'La' + noun to say 'no time / no exercise' where Levantine uses ما عندي / ما في; Amal let it pass.
